findings.title: Notification badge fill no longer contrasts with its text on dark themes
findings.body: .badge-notification keeps color: $secondary (and the same on &[href]), but its background is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). In a dark scheme $secondary is the dark page background, so the dark branch paints dark text on a background only 30% lighter than that same color, about 2:1, which is unreadable at 11px. The old scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) stayed near-white on dark themes because $primary is already light, and that light fill is what contrasted with $secondary text. The muted-text complement (lighten $secondary) is the wrong transform for a fill whose foreground is $secondary; dark themes need a light background here, or the text color has to move to $primary as well.

findings.title: Embedded post author link lightness was inverted
findings.body: .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). Every other conversion in this change keeps the original lightness on $primary for light themes and uses the complement (100 minus that lightness) on $secondary for dark themes. Light themes therefore jump from a 30% lift (a readable dark gray, roughly 6:1 on white) to a 70% lift (about #bdbdbd, under 2:1), so author names in expanded and embedded posts wash out. Dark themes get only a 30% lift of the dark background instead of 70%, so those links are darker than intended. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)), matching .names a in common/base/topic-post.scss.

findings.title: Disabled mobile composer text fails contrast on dark themes
findings.body: .wmd-input:disabled background is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 75%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 25%)), while the .wmd-input color rule immediately below stays darken($primary, 40%). On a dark scheme $primary is light, so darkening it by 40% yields a mid-dark gray, and lightening dark $secondary by 25% is another dark gray (about 1.6:1). The previous background, scale-color($primary, $lightness: 75%), was near-white when $primary is light, so the same text was readable. Desktop already styles this disabled field with dark-light-diff($primary, $secondary, 90%, -60%) and composer text as $primary. The same dark-theme background is also applied to #reply-title:disabled at line 168, which has no theme-aware text color in this file.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: .topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). That neither preserves the light-theme value nor applies the 80% complement used for a 20% source. Desktop .topic-map h3 in this same change was correctly converted to 20%/80%, and the mobile h4 immediately below was already 50% — this value looks copied from h4. Light-theme topic-map headings become much more muted than before and than desktop; dark themes use a 50% lift instead of 80%, so the heading is darker against the dark map background than the desktop rule.

findings.title: Mobile flag-message length hint lightness was swapped
findings.body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The light and dark percentages are transposed. Desktop desktop/modal.scss converts the same hint to 70% on $primary and 30% on $secondary. Light themes therefore show a darker, more prominent character-count hint than before and than desktop; dark themes lighten $secondary by 70% instead of 30%, so the hint is far brighter than the muted treatment this change is supposed to produce.

findings.title: Group member name color was given the title's lightness
findings.body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), identical to the adjacent .title, which really was 50% and was converted correctly. Light-theme names become lighter than before and no longer darker than titles; dark themes get a 50% lift of $secondary instead of 70%, so names are darker than the complement of the original 30%. common/base/user.scss still maps the parallel .name to 30%/70%. This rule should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

findings.title: Mobile group member name color was given the title's lightness
findings.body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now 50%/50%, the same value applied to .title (which was already 50%). The conversion used everywhere else keeps the original lightness for light themes and uses 100 minus that lightness on $secondary for dark themes, so this should be 30%/70%. Light-theme group-member names become lighter and indistinguishable from titles; dark themes render them darker than the intended complement. The same mistake is in desktop/user.scss, while common/base/user.scss still uses 30%/70% for .name.

findings.title: Category badge count still lightens $primary on dark themes
findings.body: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still sets color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) on a transparent background. Every other positive scale-color($primary, $lightness: …) in this file was wrapped as dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, …), scale-color($secondary, …)). On a dark scheme $primary is already light, so a further 50% lightness scale pushes the count toward white instead of the muted gray used for topic-list headers and excerpts (50%/50%). Category notification counts stay brighter than the surrounding muted text this change is fixing.
